title: PRISMA-style flow diagram
what: How many records each step of the search, de-duplication, screening and snowballing kept or removed.
how: Counts logged by python/pipeline.py (tables/prisma_counts.csv); blue = kept, red = removed.
caution: Screening was rule-based (regular expressions on title and abstract) plus one hand pass by an AI agent over titles; it is not a double-blind human screen, so treat the corpus as a map, not a systematic review.

title: Publications by year and sub-literature
what: Top: stacked count of corpus documents per year by sub-literature. Bottom: each sub-literature's share of that year's documents.
how: master.csv; sub-literature = first inclusion rule matched. matplotlib.
caution: The mix depends on how many queries each sub-literature had and on the per-query caps; the latest year is incomplete.

title: Timeline of key papers
what: The 28 corpus documents most cited by other corpus documents, in order of publication, coloured by sub-literature.
how: Local citations from exact OpenAlex reference matching (citation_edges.csv); ties broken by global citations.
caution: Recent papers have had little time to be cited, so the list under-represents work from the last two or three years - which for fast-moving topics is where the key papers are.

title: Database overlap
what: Left: how many final-corpus records each discovery source retrieved. Right: the most common combinations of sources per record.
how: 'found_in' field of master.csv (which searches returned the record before OpenAlex enrichment).
caution: Low overlap is expected: each database was queried with different syntax and per-query caps, so this is not a measure of database quality.

title: Author-country map (interactive)
what: Choropleth of the number of corpus documents with at least one author affiliated in each country.
how: OpenAlex authorship country codes; plotly choropleth, self-contained HTML.
caution: Shows where authors are employed, not which countries are studied; records without affiliations (many Indian-journal and legal records) are not on the map.

title: Geography of study settings
what: How many corpus documents name each country in the title or abstract - a rough proxy for where the evidence comes from.
how: Case-insensitive name matching (with a few aliases such as 'American', 'British') on title + abstract in master.csv.
caution: A name in an abstract is not the same as a study setting (it can be a comparison or an author address), and India is partly a search term here, so its bar is inflated by design.

title: Direct citation network (static)
what: Corpus documents (nodes) joined when one cites the other, coloured by sub-literature; shows whether the sub-literatures cite each other or sit apart.
how: Exact matches between OpenAlex referenced_works and corpus ids; up to 350 most connected documents; networkx spring layout, seed 7.
caution: Missing links are common for books, working papers and journals without deposited reference lists - an isolated node may be un-indexed rather than uncited.

title: Direct citation network (interactive)
what: The same network as the PNG, interactive: hover a node for title, authors, source, citation counts and DOI.
how: pyvis / vis.js, self-contained HTML (opens offline in any browser); Barnes-Hut physics layout.
caution: The layout is a physics simulation and differs on every load; only the links are data.

title: Citation flows between sub-literatures
what: Number of within-corpus citation links from documents of one sub-literature (rows) to another (columns). A strong diagonal with weak off-diagonal cells means the sub-literatures are separate conversations.
how: citation_edges.csv cross-tabulated by the sub-literature of citing and cited document.
caution: Cell sizes also reflect how many documents each sub-literature has and how well its sources deposit reference lists; compare proportions, not raw counts.

title: Main path / key-route view
what: The chain of papers that the largest number of citation paths run through - a summary of the field's main line of development.
how: Search path count (SPC) on the acyclic within-corpus citation network (links against time order removed); key-route search from the 8 highest-SPC links, extended greedily backward and forward (Liu & Lu key-route approach). networkx.
caution: The main path follows the best-connected thread, which is the best-indexed sub-literature; a missing topic may only mean its papers do not cite each other in indexed sources.

title: Co-citation network of references (Python)
what: Works that corpus documents cite together, grouped into Louvain clusters - the intellectual bases of the literature, with readable author-year labels.
how: Co-citation counts over OpenAlex referenced_works of all corpus records; 150 most cited references clustered (networkx Louvain, seed 3), 70 drawn; spring layout, seed 11. Cluster membership: tables/py_cocitation_clusters.csv.
caution: Cluster boundaries move with the resolution parameter and the 150-reference cut-off; read the clusters as rough schools, not fixed categories.

title: Co-citation of references - VOSviewer layout
what: Co-citation of references map positioned and clustered by VOSviewer 1.6.20 itself (VOS mapping + VOS clustering), then drawn with matplotlib because the VOSviewer command line cannot export images.
how: VOSviewer.exe -map/-network -run_layout -run_clustering -save_map on vosviewer/py_cocitation_references_map.txt and _network.txt; default VOSviewer parameters.
caution: Closeness means relatedness only approximately (a 2-D projection); open the map and network files in the VOSviewer GUI to inspect links and change resolution.

title: Keyword co-occurrence - VOSviewer layout
what: Keyword co-occurrence map positioned and clustered by VOSviewer 1.6.20 itself (VOS mapping + VOS clustering), then drawn with matplotlib because the VOSviewer command line cannot export images.
how: VOSviewer.exe -map/-network -run_layout -run_clustering -save_map on vosviewer/keyword_cooccurrence_map.txt and _network.txt; default VOSviewer parameters.
caution: Closeness means relatedness only approximately (a 2-D projection); open the map and network files in the VOSviewer GUI to inspect links and change resolution.

title: Co-authorship (authors) - VOSviewer layout
what: Co-authorship (authors) map positioned and clustered by VOSviewer 1.6.20 itself (VOS mapping + VOS clustering), then drawn with matplotlib because the VOSviewer command line cannot export images.
how: VOSviewer.exe -map/-network -run_layout -run_clustering -save_map on vosviewer/coauthorship_authors_map.txt and _network.txt; default VOSviewer parameters.
caution: Closeness means relatedness only approximately (a 2-D projection); open the map and network files in the VOSviewer GUI to inspect links and change resolution.

title: Keyword burst timeline (Kleinberg)
what: Years in which a keyword (or OpenAlex topic where a record has no keywords) appears in more corpus records than its overall share predicts.
how: Kleinberg two-state automaton per keyword, yearly slots, s=2, gamma=1, keywords with at least 4 records (top 80 by frequency); ranked by excess count; table tables/py_burst_keywords.csv. Own Python implementation of the batch version.
caution: Small yearly counts make bursts fragile and the keywords are machine-assigned (OpenAlex), not author-chosen; a burst in the corpus can come from my search terms or snowballing rather than from the field.

title: Reference burst timeline (Kleinberg)
what: Years in which a heavily cited corpus paper receives more citations from other corpus papers than its overall share predicts.
how: Kleinberg two-state automaton, yearly slots, s=2, gamma=1, on the 40 most cited-within-corpus works; citing years from citation_edges.csv; table tables/py_burst_references.csv.
caution: Only citations from inside the corpus count, so a burst shows what this map's papers cite, not total citation history; counts per year are small.

title: Main path of the citation network
what: The chain of papers that carries the most citation traffic from earliest to latest work inside the corpus.
how: Search path count weights on the citation DAG (edges oriented cited to citing, same-year cycles broken); global main path maximises total weight; key-route list (top 14 edges extended both ways, 36 papers) in tables/py_mainpath_keyroute.csv; papers on the global path in tables/py_mainpath_global.csv.
caution: Only citations between corpus papers count; the path is sensitive to which papers the search and snowball retrieved, and to the many papers outside the largest component that are left out.

title: Methods against markets and datasets
what: Count of corpus records whose title or abstract names each method (rows) together with each market or dataset type (columns). Empty or low cells show method-market pairings the corpus rarely contains, for example high-frequency retail bid-only data.
how: Case-insensitive regular expressions on title+abstract of master.csv records that have an abstract (patterns in python/topic_chart_03.py); coded records in tables/py_method_market_coded_records.csv.
caution: Keyword coding, not reading: a mention is not a use, a record can sit in several cells, and records without abstracts are dropped, so low counts partly reflect missing abstracts and the search terms.
